heading: Delivery and migration
body: Payloads are model values that travel as finite JSON of at most 64 KiB. Each listener gets its own copy. Delivery has limits on listeners, queues and cycles. A republished event has the same limits. Events are not transactional, and they are not a background-job API. Tachyon saves only the events of a Topic model, in the topic log (see Topics); other events are not durable. The EventPublisher annotation, the this.tac object, the TacRuntime type and the implicit mount hook are removed. Instead, inject the applicationEventPublisher. Use HTTPClient and request annotations, the lifecycle and listener markers and the injected resources. ty migrate reports an EventPublisher method as Changed. It names the injected publisher that replaces it. Cleanup runs once. It runs when the user leaves the page, on hot replacement, or when the document is really removed. In hot replacement, the development server swaps in changed code. A prototype-scoped service gets a new instance each time it is injected. For such a service, cleanup runs when its component is removed. When the browser suspends the page in its back-forward cache (bfcache), Tachyon keeps the owner. String event names are removed (ADR 0055): OnEvent takes no event or events, and publishEvent takes no name. ty migrate fix --write converts listeners, and JavaScript and TypeScript calls, whose event name matches a model, and lists the rest as manual steps. Ruby listeners name their model in a YARD tag, # @param order [PlacedOrder], and the fix converts a Ruby listener that already has that tag.
